title: Planner overrides as bounds

blocks.text: This is the mock's whiteboard, coded. A port authority's planners override the optimizer, and one built model must serve every what-if. `overrides.py` already has a start variable `x[(pid, year)]` for each project and each year in its window, and the row that each project starts at most once. Write `apply_overrides(model, x, projects, overrides)` for four kinds of override:

items: `("start_in", pid, year)`: the project is funded and starts in that year;
`("never", pid)`: the project is not funded;
`("not_before", pid, year)`: if the project is funded, it starts in that year or later;
`("fund", pid)`: the project is funded, in any year of its window.

blocks.text: Use variable bounds wherever one bound per variable can say the override, and a row only where it cannot.
Check the overrides before any solve, and raise `ValueError` for two kinds that can never hold:

items: a `start_in` year outside the project's window (there is no variable for it);

overrides that contradict each other on one variable, leaving its lower bound above its upper bound (`start_in` and `never` on the same project, say). MathOpt refuses to solve a model with such a variable, so the clash is reported here, by name, instead. Write down, for each override, which bounds move or which labelled row is added before you code it.

blocks.text: The tests fix plans and ask HiGHS whether the model allows them, so any correct formulation passes. About twenty lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from overrides import Project, build

projects = [Project("D1", (2031, 2032, 2033)), Project("D2", (2031, 2032)), Project("D3", (2032, 2033))]


def bounds(overrides):
    try:
        model, x = build(projects, overrides)
    except ValueError as error:
        return f"refused: {error}"
    rows = [c.name for c in model.linear_constraints()]
    return {f"{p} {t}": (v.lower_bound, v.upper_bound) for (p, t), v in x.items()}, rows


print("start_in D1 2032, never D2:", bounds([("start_in", "D1", 2032), ("never", "D2")]))
print("not_before D1 2033, fund D3:", bounds([("not_before", "D1", 2033), ("fund", "D3")]))
print("start_in D2 2033:", bounds([("start_in", "D2", 2033)]))
print("start_in D3 2032, never D3:", bounds([("start_in", "D3", 2032), ("never", "D3")]))

cases.says: a project overridden to start in a year may not start in another
a project overridden to never be funded is refused in any year
a not-before override refuses a start before its year
a fund override refuses a plan that leaves the project out
a start-in override refuses a plan that leaves the project out
a not-before override allows a start in its own year
a fund override allows the project in any year of its window
a start-in override outside the project's window is refused before the solve
two overrides that leave a lower bound above its upper bound are refused before the solve

concepts: turn planner overrides into variable bounds and one row, and refuse overrides that cannot hold
